title: Social Security Payments Will Go Up 3.6 Percent
summary:
Many older Americans will get a raise next year. Social Security payments will go up by 3.6 percent in 2027. The Associated Press says this adds up to a little more than $900 next year.

Social Security is a government program. It sends monthly money to people who are 62 or older and to people with a disability or blindness.

Every year, the raise is set by a math formula called the cost-of-living adjustment, or COLA. It is tied to inflation, which is when prices go up. When prices rise a lot, the raise is bigger. The new amount starts in January.

Expert Shai Akabas said this year's raise is "not wildly outside of the norm."

Experts said the raise may not feel the same for everyone. Older people often spend more on health care. People who drive a lot may also feel it is not enough because gas prices are high.
why_it_matters: Many grandparents rely on Social Security, so this raise helps them pay for food and other needs as prices rise.
